text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Secondary school pupils beat up their teacher and a fellow pupil after a basketball match in Limassol.
- If international crude prices drop to or below 20 dollars per barrel retail fuel prices will not go up.
- President Glafcos Clerides accuses top brass in police of a coverup of crimes committed by police officers last year.
- Deputy police chief minces his words when asked to clarify why he tape recorded police officers last year who allegedly confessed to their involvement in organised crime.

- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash is willing to allow Greek Cypriot refugees to return to their land in the Turkish zone in the event of a federation, but will adopt a 'fishnet policy' to keep large landowners out.
- Cypriot authorities will create a unit to fight money laundering.
- Members of the electricity authority board sacked over allegations of irregularities in endorsing a generator tender are taking the government to court.
- Worrying messages reach Nicosia and Athens that some European countries may try to impose a solution to the Cyprus problem if it is not settled before accession negotiations start.
